newsitem.title: USA: Spier reiterates request Video review offer.
newsitem.headline: Spier reiterates request Video review offer.

text.p: New York Investor William Spier said Thursday he wrote Video Lottery Technologies Inc asking the board's special committee to make a decision regarding his $6 per common share proposal to acquire the company.

Spier disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission that he wrote Richard Burt, chairman of the board's special committee on December 31 requesting the committee promptly respond to the proposal.

Spier, who is a director of Video Lottery, heads a group that holds a 14.4 percent stake in Video or 1,496,564 common shares. He also offered to buy another 20 percent of Video's shares for $6 per share immediately upon the signing of an agreement.

Spier wrote he submitted a "no lose" proposal to the Atlanta, Ga., based company and "after signing an agreement for my transaction...VLT will be free to continue to pursue alternatives producing greater cash value."
"If I am unable to close my proposed transaction, I will reimburse VLT's expenses," Spier wrote. "VLT will not be out-of-pocket anything."
Video provides terminals, software and services to the video lottery market. With about 10.7 million shares outstanding, the Spier bid is worth about $64.2 million.
In the letter Spier objected to any attempt to deprive him of his ability to perform his duties as a director under the "guise of establishing a fair bidding process."
"I do not want any information regarding the activities of other bidders, if there are any, of the deliberations of the Special Committee regarding sales of businessess or the company."
